title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A guide to writing code that other people can read and change: naming, small functions, error handling and tests.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andy Hunt, Dave Thomas
description: Practical habits for working programmers, from avoiding duplication to automating what you repeat.

title: Effective Java
author: Joshua Bloch
description: Concrete advice on using Java well, organised as short items on objects, generics, lambdas and concurrency.

title: Head first Java
author: Kathy Sierra
description: A visual, exercise-heavy introduction to Java and object-oriented programming for beginners.

title: Design Patterns
author: Erich Gamma, John Vlissides
description: The catalogue of classic object-oriented design patterns, each with its intent, structure and trade-offs.

title: Refactoring
author: Martin Fowler
description: How to improve the design of existing code in small, safe steps without changing what it does.

title: Code Complete
author: Steve McConnell
description: A broad handbook of software construction: design, variables, control flow, debugging and code quality.

title: Eloquent Javascript
author: Marijn Haverbeke
description: An introduction to programming through JavaScript, covering the language, the browser and Node.

title: Python Crash Course, 2nd Edition
author: Eric Matthes
description: A fast, project-based introduction to Python for people who have never programmed before.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
author: Al Sweigart
description: Python for everyday tasks: working with files, spreadsheets, web pages and repetitive chores.

title: The C Programming Language
author: Brian W. Kernighan, Dennis MacAlistair Ritchie
description: The concise reference and tutorial for the C language, written by its creators.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (SICP)
author: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman
description: A foundational text on how programs are built from abstractions, taught through Scheme.

title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson
description: A comprehensive textbook on algorithms and data structures with proofs and pseudocode.

title: Algorithms
author: Robert Sedgewick
description: Algorithms and data structures explained with working Java implementations and clear diagrams.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz
description: How operating systems work: processes, memory, storage, scheduling and protection.

title: Artificial intelligence
author: Stuart J. Russell, Peter Norvig
description: The standard university introduction to artificial intelligence, from search to learning.

title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
author: Randal E. Bryant, David R. O'Hallaron
description: What happens underneath a program: machine code, memory, linking, processes and networking.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: How databases and distributed systems store, replicate and process data, and the trade-offs involved.

title: Cracking The Coding Interview
author: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
description: Practice problems and explanations for data-structure and algorithm interview questions.

title: Calculus
author: James Stewart
description: A widely used calculus textbook covering limits, derivatives, integrals and series with many exercises.

title: Linear Algebra Done Right
author: Sheldon Jay Axler
description: A proof-based second course in linear algebra that builds the subject around linear maps.

title: How to solve it
author: George Pólya
description: A short classic on problem-solving method: understand, plan, carry out, look back.

title: Concrete mathematics
author: Ronald L. Graham, Donald Knuth
description: The mathematics behind computer science: sums, recurrences, number theory and generating functions.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
author: Kenneth H. Rosen
description: Logic, sets, counting, graphs and proofs: the discrete mathematics used across computing courses.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: A popular account of cosmology, black holes and the nature of time for general readers.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: A tour of the universe and the history of science, written for a general audience.

title: Thinking, fast and slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: How two modes of thinking shape judgement and decisions, drawn from decades of psychology research.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
description: An approach to building products by testing assumptions early with small experiments.

title: Zero to One
author: Peter A. Thiel, Blake Masters
description: Notes on startups and building companies that create something new.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt, Stephen J. Dubner
description: Economics applied to everyday puzzles, with an emphasis on incentives and data.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
description: A dystopian novel about surveillance, propaganda and the control of truth.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: A novel of childhood and injustice in the American South, told through a young girl's eyes.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: A novel of manners about marriage, family and first impressions in Regency England.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: A novel of wealth, longing and illusion set in 1920s New York.
